elements.evidence: Operation deletes p0013 in its entirety; the rendered clause is empty, so no 'sole and exclusive provider' language remains.

elements.element: No 'sole supplier' / requirements commitment on Customer (preferred)
elements.evidence: Deleted text 'Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.' no longer operative; official check confirms 'no requirements/sole-supplier obligation on Customer remains'.

reasons: Locked target is preferred, and the preferred position (no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Customer) is fully achieved by deleting the only sentence imposing it.
The fallback bargain is not satisfied and does not need to be; the drafter correctly offers it only in the non-operative margin comment.

On minimality, the paragraph consisted solely of the offending exclusivity commitment ('Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider ... throughout the term.'); there was no unrelated commercial term to preserve, so deletion changes no more than necessary. The official minimality gate's whole-paragraph flag is not substantively offending here.

Intent preserved: no defined term is orphaned and no cross-reference depends on the deleted sentence; Sections 2.1 and 12.3 (no purchase commitment or exclusivity) remain consistent and no dangling mechanic is created.
